dedupe_keys.name: dgm w elbe 2022 digital terrain and surface models of the elbe and lower havel watercourses and floodplains bfg

description: The DGM-W Elbe 2022 is a 1 m digital terrain model of the Elbe from the Czech-German border to Zollenspieker in Hamburg and of the Lower Havel waterway from Rathenow to the Elbe, combining the land surface with the bed of rivers, channels and lakes; a companion digital surface model (DOM1) covers the same 4,043 km2. It merges airborne laser scanning of 2021 and 2022, multibeam and multi-channel echo sounding, bathymetric laser scanning of 2018 and models of constructions, split into 62 sections marked as flood-relevant areas or historical floodplains, with source-flag maps for quality assessment. Germany's Federal Institute of Hydrology (BfG) produced it for the River Basin Community Elbe with the Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration and the surveying and water offices of six states. Coverage is regional, the German Elbe and Lower Havel corridor. Both models are a free download from Zenodo as GeoTIFF sections (about 12 GB and 11 GB) under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the files are large, gaps are filled by substitute models or interpolation, and the data describe terrain, not flood defence assets as such. Simulation uses: river and floodplain geometry for hydraulic and flood modelling, water level forecasting and exposure of waterway and flood infrastructure. Related records: none catalogued yet.
